question: Flash-loan liquidity for (a) a borrow-gOHM path and (b) a buy path (stables), and whether a flash loan enables a spot crash.

flash_available.note: Balancer/Morpho add more; stables are effectively unbounded (billions) for a flash path

ohm_or_gohm_flash.any_protocol: none - no lending market lists OHM or gOHM (see cross_protocol.json), so there is no OHM/gOHM flash-loan source

why_flash_cannot_crash: To push a price DOWN you must SELL the base asset (OHM/gOHM). A flash loan provides the QUOTE asset (USDC/USDS/WETH); spending it BUYS OHM and pushes the price UP, not down.
There is no OHM/gOHM flash source, so the attacker cannot flash-borrow the inventory needed to dump.

Even with OHM inventory, a flash crash + buy-back is a round trip: the same AMM the attacker dumped into is the only buyer, so the buy-back pays the impact + 2x fees (measured: -$4,213 / -0.70% on a 40k OHM round trip).

Cooler's oracle reads no market price, so there is nothing to manipulate; no third-party oracle reads the crashed spot (the only gOHM oracle, Inverse FiRM, is a Chainlink feed and its market is paused).
conclusion: Flash-loan spot manipulation is DEFINITIVELY not viable for this finding. Quote-asset flash depth (billions) is irrelevant because the binding constraint is OHM/gOHM inventory, which cannot be flash-borrowed.
